title: Spectral Loom
pages: Craft this t6 controller with two Refracted Matrix, two white wool, a loom, a Solenoid in the centre, a Solar Prism etched in the Heliostat Etcher and two Coil Springs in the bottom corners. The Solenoid is the hook-selection actuator, as electronic Jacquard heads lift each warp hook with a short-stroke electromagnet; a scaffolding block, a bare Soft-Iron Plunger or a loose Wound Coil cannot replace it. Make it from four iron ingots (the magnetic C-frame), a Wound Coil from the Induction Coiler, a Soft-Iron Plunger and a Coil Spring that returns the plunger when the coil is off. For the plunger, draw one tagged iron ingot into a Drawn Iron Rod on the Wire Drawing Bench, then anneal it in the Induction Coiler: cold drawing hardens iron, and annealing makes it magnetically soft again so the plunger releases cleanly. Pull force, stroke, duty cycle and coil heating are not simulated. The springs return the heddle treadles after each pick, as real loom treadles are sprung back; wool cannot replace them. Draw them on the Wire Drawing Bench: one Tool Steel Stock gives four springs. Real springs are cold-coiled from hardened, drawn wire and then stress relieved at about 200-315 C to remove coiling stress; the bench abstracts coiling, stress relief and spring rate. The prism commits the textile branch to t6 before its Woven Sigil is bound in a Reliquary Stand, sealed at a Concordance Altar, and keyed in an Iridescent Basin.

Place a loom below, a scaffolding block above, white wool north and south, and cobwebs east and west, then lay a stripped oak log warp beam on top of each cobweb. All eight parts must remain in place. Right-click with a full input batch; breaking any arm stops production.

Sixteen dye batches weave each vanilla dye directly into eight blocks of matching colored wool, skipping the usual wool cost. Sixteen more batches weave four colored wool into eight matching colored carpet. A fusion batch compresses two Refracted Matrix into a Lumen Filament for the next t5 controller.

Right-click with a full batch for direct hand feeding. For automation, insert recipe inputs through the top or horizontal controller faces and extract finished textiles from the bottom; each port exposes one slot. The two-slot buffer persists through save/load and drops its contents if broken. Processing pauses when any frame block is missing or output is full. No FE or fluid port is needed. JEI shows loaded batches; matching ties resolve by resource ID.
